name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Rebuilt the Federation settings page from scratch around one simple flow instead of two confusing ones. Adding a friend used to mean either a clean URL-only handshake or an older path where you had to copy an API key by hand from the other server's Dashboard - the key-paste path and its "Remote user" dropdown are gone; there's just one "type their server address" flow now, and the account used to pull a friend's library is resolved automatically the same way playback already did. Per-friend sharing (what a friend can see of your library) and pools are promoted out of a stack of buried, nested disclosures into a real "People" panel per friend.

Added "download to server": on a federated item's detail page, a Download button fetches the file from the friend's server and saves it locally, so it plays back afterward with no dependency on their server being online - it becomes a completely ordinary local item once the next library scan picks it up. Also added a way to add an already-connected friend straight into a pool (no re-typing their address).

Added an origin filter for library grids and search results: a small floating "Origin filter" control (reusing the same data the corner/pill badges already fetch) lists local content plus every friend server seen so far, each with a checkbox - uncheck a server to hide its items from the current view, or uncheck everything except one to see only that server's content. The choice is remembered across navigation via localStorage. It's a standalone control rather than a hook into jellyfin-web's native filter dialog, since that dialog's internal markup isn't something this plugin can safely target from outside a jellyfin-web fork.

Added a local "Hide" action for federated items: on a federated item's detail page, a Hide button (next to Download) removes it from your own library browsing/search/home going forward - useful for a friend's low-quality rip of something you already own in better quality, or content you just don't want cluttering your library. This is purely local: the friend is never notified and keeps sharing normally, and it's unrelated to per-friend sharing permissions (which control what a friend can see of *your* content, the opposite direction). Manage and unhide previously-hidden items from a new "Hidden items" section on the settings page; an unhidden item reappears on the next sync.

Added per-remote-user access overrides: the People panel for each friend now lists that friend's own local user accounts (fetched live from their server), and clicking one lets you block them entirely, narrow them to a subset of the libraries already shared with that friend, or narrow them all the way down to specific items - layered on top of the existing per-friend sharing scope, never widening it. Since a friend's whole server queries under one shared account today, there was no way for a friend's admin to distinguish which of their own users was asking; the rule you set is now pushed to the friend's own plugin, which enforces it locally against whichever of their users is actually browsing or streaming, re-checked again at the moment a Proxy-mode stream is requested. No rule configured (the common case) behaves exactly as before. Item-level picking reuses a new minimal local item search endpoint since none existed on this page yet.

Fixed federated items being invisible to Jellyfin's own Continue Watching, Latest, and library-browsing queries even though playback itself worked fine. Root cause: federated items have no real file behind them (their Path is a URL on the friend's server), so their library's on-disk shadow folder is always genuinely empty - and Jellyfin's own library scan refuses to register a physical Folder for an empty folder, skipping it as "inaccessible or empty" instead. Without that physical Folder, federated items ended up parented directly to the library itself, and every query Jellyfin runs by ancestor/top-parent (Continue Watching, Latest, Recommended, browsing the library, any Home screen widget) resolves that parent to zero physical folders and comes back empty - confirmed against a live server: the item was always still reachable by its own id (direct fetch, PlaybackInfo, the Sessions/Now Playing panel while actively playing), just invisible to anything that lists by library. A hidden marker file dropped into each federation library's shadow folder keeps it non-empty, so Jellyfin registers a real physical Folder for it exactly like any other library, and federated items become visible everywhere a local item would be, including their resume position after playback stops. Existing installations self-heal on upgrade: provisioning now also backfills the marker into already-created shadow folders and prompts a library scan so previously-affected items are picked up without waiting on the next scheduled one.

194 tests (up from 192).
